subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Heterogeneous collection of low-level runtime helpers with mostly unknown owners: empty no-op callback stubs (nullsub_*), forwarding thunks and trampolines, tiny integer/character predicates, byte-flag setters, complementary bit-mask layout translation helpers, and CRT floating-point formatting helpers. Grouped into a small number of GUESS classes by shared caller evidence; the bulk of functions remain unowned.

summary: This packet is a grab-bag of generic runtime objects rather than a coherent subsystem. Of the 39 functions, 14 are empty no-op stubs (nullsub_*) with no behavior and no recorded callers, 5 are sentinel/constant stubs (return -1, 0, 1024, 16-bit -1), and 4 are forwarding thunks or trampolines whose targets are named only in raw source text. The only evidence-backed structure is three small clusters sharing callers: (1) a file-data processing path where FileDataProcessor (0x00567FB0) invokes two forwarding thunks (0x00567AF0, 0x00567B00) and a character-class predicate (0x005678F0) is used by the forwarded target sub_567B10; (2) a complementary bit-mask translation pair (0x005950A3, 0x00595135) both invoked by BitFieldMaskMerge (0x00595058); and (3) CRT floating-point formatting helpers (0x0059086E, 0x00590703, 0x0059567D) invoked by CRT float-display and locale-aware formatting callers. These three clusters are proposed as GUESS classes; all other functions are left with UnknownObject ownership and their contracts recorded as concrete observable constants.

classes.name: FileDataProcessingHelpers
classes.responsibility: Forwarding thunks and a character-class predicate on the file-data processing path. FileDataProcessor (0x00567FB0) invokes the two thunks directly (0x00567AF0 forwards to sub_567B10, 0x00567B00 forwards to sub_567AF0); the predicate 0x005678F0 is used by caller sub_567B10, the forwarded target. Grouping is by shared caller evidence, not proven ownership.

classes.name: BitMaskTranslation
classes.responsibility: Complementary pair of bit-mask layout translation helpers invoked by BitFieldMaskMerge (0x00595058). They remap individual bit positions between two mask layouts and are a near-inverse over the shared low bits (bit 1 is ignored by one direction).

classes.name: CRTFloatFormatting
classes.responsibility: Helpers on CRT floating-point formatting paths: double load/validation (CRTFloatLoad, 0x0059086E), frame-flag clearing before delegation (0x00590703), and double-to-extended-precision conversion (0x0059567D) used by a locale-aware string formatter. The first two share the CRT float-display callers; the third sits on a separate formatting caller path and is grouped here only as a GUESS.

compatibility_contracts.name: MaskTranslationContract
compatibility_contracts.description: The two bit-mask translation helpers must preserve the observed bit mappings: bitMaskRemapA maps input bits 0,2,3,4,5 to output values 16,8,4,2,1 (input bit 1 ignored); bitMaskRemapB maps input bits 4,3,2,1,0,19 to output values 1,4,8,16,32,2. The pair is a near-inverse over the shared low bits.

compatibility_contracts.name: ConstantGetters1024
compatibility_contracts.description: Two callables return the fixed integer 1024 with no arguments and no side effects. A replacement must preserve this constant for consumers such as the wrapper at 0x0057A750.

compatibility_contracts.name: StatusSentinelStubs
compatibility_contracts.description: Stubs return fixed status sentinels: GetFailureCode variants return -1 (0x00598CCF, 0x00598CD8), GetSuccessCode returns 0 (0x00598CD5), and sub_599D25/sub_599D2C return 16-bit -1. A replacement preserving these callable slots must keep the sentinel values.

compatibility_contracts.name: CharacterClassPredicate
compatibility_contracts.description: A predicate returns TRUE exactly when its unsigned byte argument is <= 0x20 (control/whitespace class); used by caller 0x00567B10 on the file-data processing path.

compatibility_contracts.name: NoOpCallbackSlots
compatibility_contracts.description: Multiple callable slots exist as empty no-ops that return with no side effects. A replacement must preserve these callable slots as side-effect-free: 0x00566B14, 0x005679B7, 0x00568314, 0x0056F0F3, 0x0057EC03, 0x005853A8, 0x00585543, 0x0058A2EE, 0x0058A7E8, 0x005910A0, 0x00598E2B, 0x0059AAA2, 0x008D8A7C, 0x008D8C2C.

unresolved: Owner and purpose of the vast majority of these functions are unknown; the packet provides no caller, callee, field, or subsystem evidence for most of them.
The three proposed classes are GUESS groupings by shared caller evidence, not proven ownership. Equal callers do not prove a common class.

The forwarding chain FileDataProcessor (0x00567FB0) -> 0x00567B00 -> sub_567AF0 -> sub_567B10 -> CharacterClassCheck (0x005678F0) is textual: sub_567AF0 and sub_567B10 are named only in raw source and have no address evidence in the packet.
Trampoline targets locret_587C99 (0x00567BA2) and SingleFunctionCallWrapper_a910 (0x0057A908) are named only in raw text; the actual delegated functions are unconfirmed.
FPUStatusErrorHandler (0x0058DD75) jumps out to 0x58DD9D whose code is outside this packet; whether it is a jump-table case, tail call, or shared block is unknown.
ClearFrameFlagAndDelegate (0x00590703) calls sub_59070A, which is absent from the packet callee evidence; its identity, arguments, and return contract are unresolved.
DualAdjacentByteWrite (0x0057A229) writes sibling byte fields at object offsets 0x2B and 0x2C, but the base object is unknown; the fields are therefore not assigned to any class.

SetByteFlag (0x0058DC29) writes byte 1 at (base - 144), a negative offset relative to an unknown base object; the offset cannot be represented as a positive field offset and the owner struct is unknown.
PARTIALCorruptedDecompilation (0x0057A0E6) has an unreliable stack model ('positive sp value'); the byte accumulation at a2 + 1583287492 is treated as a decompilation artifact, not a real field.
callThroughReturnAddress (0x0056A23A) is likely a compiler artifact or custom call thunk; the far-pointer target constructed from the saved return address cannot be resolved statically.
Two identical GetFailureCode stubs (0x00598CCF, 0x00598CD8) and the adjacent sentinel pair sub_599D25/sub_599D2C: whether they are independent stubs or aliases to one intent is not established.
The semantic meaning of the constant 1024 (buffer size, allocation quantum, count) returned by 0x00587890 and 0x0058792A is unknown.
NodeCountCheck (0x0056F80B) validates its argument against 40, and EnumValueCheck (0x00575875) against 34, but the node collection and the enumeration are unidentified.

convertDoubleToExtended80 (0x0059567D): the legacy ABI labels imply an 80-bit to 64-bit direction, but the raw code reads a 64-bit double and writes a 10-byte extended value; the direction discrepancy is unresolved.
CRTFloatLoad (0x0059086E): the all-ones exponent special path (NaN/Inf re-normalization) purpose is unconfirmed and the CRT___fload ABI lead is LEGACY trust only.
CharacterClassCheck (0x005678F0): whether the class is whitespace, control, or terminator is inferred from the 0x20 bound only; the exact class is unconfirmed.
The __userpurge/EBX and __fastcall argument conventions used by some functions are assumed from decompiler prototypes; register placement is not verified.
